skill.name: wizard
skill.description: Generate interactive Bash setup wizards for manual workflows that open URLs, collect values, write environment files, and set GitHub secrets.
skill.summary: Build guided Bash scripts for setup, migrations, and project state changes.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: Most static command and filesystem findings are false positives from Markdown inline code, terminal formatting, arithmetic expansion, browser-opening helpers, and /dev/null redirection. The confirmed risk is intentional sensitive data handling: generated wizards can read .env files, collect API secrets, write them locally, and set GitHub Actions secrets.

remediation.issue: Generated wizards collect and persist API secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Keep generated scripts reviewable, use ask_secret for every secret, and warn users before writing secrets to .env or GitHub Actions.

remediation.issue: Environment files may be read or rewritten during reruns.
remediation.suggestion: Validate key names before grep and write_env, preserve file permissions, and remind users to keep .env files out of version control.

remediation.issue: External browser and gh CLI operations are part of the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Show every URL and secret target clearly before action, and require confirmation before irreversible or remote changes.

content.value_statement: Manual setup work is easy to miss, repeat, or explain poorly. This skill creates guided Bash wizards that collect values and save them consistently.
actual_capabilities: Creates interactive Bash wizard scripts from manual setup or migration steps.
Uses a reusable template with stages, progress, confirmations, and clear prompts.
Opens setup URLs through common desktop and WSL browser commands.
Captures visible values and hidden secrets from the user.
Writes values to .env files and GitHub Actions secrets or variables.
Guides static verification with bash -n and optional shellcheck.
limitations: Generated scripts require human input and are not meant for unattended automation.
The template includes secret handling, so users must review scripts before running them.
Exact third-party UI steps may need documentation checks or user confirmation.
GitHub secret and variable writes require an installed and authenticated gh CLI.

use_cases.title: Onboard a New Developer
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable setup wizard that gathers required local values and stores them in the expected environment file.

use_cases.title: Configure CI Secrets
use_cases.description: Guide a human through provider dashboards, then write only required values to GitHub Actions secrets or variables.

use_cases.title: Run a One-Time Migration
use_cases.description: Turn a fragile manual transition into staged prompts with confirmations before sensitive or irreversible steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Setup Wizard
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wizard skill to create a Bash setup wizard for this project. Inspect README files and .env examples, then propose the stages before writing the script.

prompt_templates.title: Add Provider Dashboard Steps
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a wizard for configuring a third-party service. Include the dashboard URL, exact human actions, captured values, and where each value is saved.

prompt_templates.title: Map CI Secret Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Review .github workflows and create a wizard that collects every required secret or variable. Use GitHub secret names that match the workflow references.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Migration Wizard
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged wizard for this one-time migration. Identify irreversible actions, add confirmation gates, and keep secret values hidden during input.

output_examples.input: Create a setup wizard for Stripe local development and CI.
output_examples.output: A Bash wizard with a Stripe API key stage, browser opening, hidden secret entry, .env writes, and a GitHub secret write.

output_examples.input: Turn our onboarding checklist into a guided script.
output_examples.output: A staged script that explains each manual step, pauses for confirmation, captures required values, and summarizes completed setup items.

output_examples.input: Prepare a migration wizard for a risky configuration change.
output_examples.output: A human-driven workflow with ordered stages, clear warnings, confirmation gates, and instructions for static verification before running.

best_practices: Review generated scripts before running them, especially stages that write secrets or modify remote settings.
Use hidden prompts for every secret and confirm each destination before persisting a value.
Run bash -n and shellcheck when available, then trace each captured value to its destination.
anti_patterns: Do not run the wizard end to end while authoring it, because it opens browsers and blocks on human input.
Do not invent dashboard paths or commands when the current provider UI is unknown.
Do not commit one-time setup scripts unless the user wants a repeatable repository workflow.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates Bash wizard scripts that guide a human through setup, migration, or project transition steps.

faq.question: Does it handle secrets?
faq.answer: Yes. The template supports hidden secret prompts, .env writes, and GitHub Actions secret writes through the gh CLI.

faq.question: Can it run without user interaction?
faq.answer: No. The wizard is designed for human-driven workflows with pauses, confirmations, and copied values.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users review before running a generated wizard?
faq.answer: They should review URLs, captured variables, .env writes, GitHub secret names, and any irreversible actions.

faq.question: When should a wizard be committed?
faq.answer: Commit it only when the setup path should be repeatable for future users of the repository.
